Question: How did the printing press change the spread of knowledge in Europe? Answer in one clear short paragraph:
The printing press changed the spread of knowledge in Europe by making it easier and faster to produce books. Before the printing press, books were handwritten, which was time-consuming and expensive. With the printing press, books could be mass-produced quickly and cheaply, making them more accessible to a wider audience. This led to an explosion of literacy and the spread of ideas throughout Europe during the Renaissance and Reformation periods.
